errors.description: Termination line of the pad-stitched chest canvas, normalised to forepart height. Drawing forepart spans y75-y1150 (height 1075); the heavy boundary under the dash-hatched canvas runs diagonally from (662,453) inboard to (912,698) outboard - from 35 percent to 58 percent of forepart height. Render forepart spans y33-y1144 (height 1111); the dense pad-stitched panel's lower edge is roughly LEVEL at y660, 56 percent throughout. The outboard end matches; the inboard end sits about 0.20 forepart-heights lower than drawn.
errors.expected: A canvas lower edge that climbs steeply as it moves inboard - deep at the outboard/armhole side at 58 percent and rising to 35 percent nearest the front edge, a clear diagonal cut-off
errors.actual: A level lower edge at 56 percent throughout
errors.correction: Render the pad-stitched chest canvas with a straight DIAGONAL lower edge: at the outboard side its hem sits just above the pocket line, and from there the edge rises steadily inboard so that beside the front-edge tape it terminates roughly one third of the way down the forepart. Show that diagonal as a cut raw canvas edge with the pad stitching running out to it.

errors.description: Legibility of the canvas cut-off. In the drawing the dash-hatched pad-stitched canvas and the coarse cross-hatched band are two clearly separated zones with a hard line between them. In the render the same pale hair-canvas material continues UNBROKEN from the pad-stitched panel down to the hem - pale-material pixels present in every sampled row from y=80 to y=1120 of an object bounded y33-y1144 - with no visible termination edge, so the panel reads as FULL canvas.
errors.expected: A visible hard boundary where the pad-stitched chest canvas stops, with plainly different material below it
errors.actual: Unbroken canvas to the hem, reading as full canvas
errors.correction: Make the chest canvas a separate, clearly bounded piece lying on top of the forepart, with its cut edge visible as a distinct raised line and a visible change of material below it - smooth, flat, stitch-free stabiliser under the cut-off versus the ribbed, densely pad-stitched canvas above it.

errors.description: Pocket aspect ratio. Drawing pocket 232 wide by 245 tall, ratio 0.95 - essentially square. Render 178 by 265, ratio 0.67 - tall portrait. Normalised to forepart height the pocket TOP matches well (0.65 drawn against 0.63) and the HEIGHT matches (0.228 against 0.239); only the width is short.
errors.expected: A pocket as wide as it is tall
errors.actual: A pocket two thirds as wide as tall
errors.correction: Widen the pocket so its horizontal span equals its vertical span, giving a square pocket whose inboard edge sits just clear of the front-edge tape.

notes:
BLUEPRINT_CONFLICT: the option label is 'Quarter Canvas' and the description says the canvas sits at 'roughly the top quarter of the front panel', but sheet 00C3 is titled 'SINGLE LAYER' - a layer-COUNT distinction, not an extent one - and its pad-stitched canvas descends to 58 percent of forepart height, which is half-canvas territory. The drawing does not depict what the label describes. Flagged rather than resolved; the drawing was used as the geometric authority.

00C3 is the ONLY canvas sheet in public/images/blueprints, while the catalog carries five distinct extent options (quarter / half / light-half / ultra-thin-half / full). One sheet cannot distinguish five extents, and it is not even drawing extent.

NOT measurable: no dimension callouts anywhere on this sheet, so no centimetre value for canvas depth, pocket size or tape width; every figure is a ratio against forepart height or assembly width. The identity of the coarse cross-hatched band (fusible? facing? shell turned back?) is not determinable from a 65KB JPEG at 1200px, so its EXTENT was graded but not its MATERIAL.
